To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mid-day enhancement of ear net photosynthesis due elevated C a was 26-58%, while stomatal conductance was reduced by 26%.
elevated C a increased the net photosynthesis of wheat ears, decreased the g s of ears and increased the contribution of ears to the grain filling in the future.
elevated CO 2 increases the contribution of ears to wheat grain filling, and that the drought tolerance of wheat ear photosynthesis is increased by elevated CO 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of elevated C a and water and N supply on the CO 2 and H 2 O exchange of wheat ears in the field.
a possible increase of wheat yield in the future under elevated atmospheric C a.
the response of net CO 2 uptake and water vapour conductance to elevated C a in the field and the role of N and water availability in this response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the enhancement of net CO 2 exchange of the ears due to C a enrichment was higher than that of flag leaves, and this effect was highest when the plants were grown under ample water and nitrogen supply, and when blowers were used for the C a - enrichment of both treatments.
the enhancement of net ear photosynthesis due to C a enrichment is restricted when water and N supply are limiting.
the effects of C a on net photosynthesis of wheat ears and g s were not altered by the N and Irr treatments but the blower effect was significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
C a enrichment increased ear net photosynthesis and reduced the sensitivity of g s to elevated C a when the water and N supply were ample.
the response of wheat ears to higher C a is not affected by the use of blowers for C a enrichment, but is affected by water and N supply.

the response of net CO 2 uptake and g s of wheat ears to higher C a depends on the interaction of water and nitrogen availability and the presence or absence of blower induced winds in the C a treatment plots.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enhancement of the ear photosynthesis by elevated C a will be more pronounced under ample soil water and N supply than in dry and/or low N environments.
the response of wheat ears to elevated atmospheric CO 1 concentration is highly dependent on the availability of water and N supply, and that this response may change with the future increase in C a.
the response of wheat ear photosynthesis and g s to elevated C a is not only dependent on the C a concentration per se, but also on the water supply and N availability.
